blocks.content: Tsunami is a Japanese word that means 'harbour wave' because the harbours get destroyed whenever there is a tsunami.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Tsunami is a Japanese word meaning 'Harbour Wave' ('tsu' meaning harbour and 'nami' meaning wave).
Tsunamis are series of massive sea waves generated by large-scale underwater disturbances such as subduction earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, or submarine landslides.
In deep ocean waters, tsunami waves travel at extremely high speeds with small wave heights, but as they reach shallow coastal waters, their speed drops and wave height grows dramatically.
The 2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami was caused by a megathrust earthquake off the western coast of Sumatra, Indonesia.
Following the 2004 disaster, India set up the Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre (ITEWC) at INCOIS in Hyderabad.
Tsunamis are seismic sea waves caused by vertical displacement of water, NOT ocean tides.
Indira Point, the southernmost point of India located in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, was submerged during the 2004 Tsunami.
Tsunami wave speed is directly proportional to the square root of water depth, making deep-water detection crucial.
